review_note: Biproduct of two diagrams in an additive idempotent-complete category has a colimit iff each diagram does, and the colimit is their biproduct. Matched against the pinned original theorem text in the Stage A source packet; did not open proof/remark text. Preliminary decision only.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{I}$ be a category. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an additive, Karoubian
category. Let $F : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{A}$ and
$G : \mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{A}$ be functors. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\colim_\mathcal{I}(F\oplus G)$ exists, and
\item $\colim_\mathcal{I} F$ and $\colim_\mathcal{I} G$ exist.
\end{enumerate}
In this case $\colim_\mathcal{I}(F\oplus G) =
\colim_\mathcal{I} F \oplus \colim_\mathcal{I} G$.
hypotheses: Let $F,G:\mathcal I\to\mathcal A$ be diagrams in an additive Karoubian category.
conclusions: The colimit of the pointwise biproduct diagram $F\oplus G$ exists iff the colimits of $F$ and $G$ both exist.
